title: Spec check: every slice has explicit, verifiable acceptance criteria
lead: *Proposed.* The spec check prompt counts a slice as ready only when its `Failing tests` and `Check` sections each say how to tell the work is done: a command the implementer's sandbox can run, with the result that means done. A slice that does not gets one owner question, with a concrete wording proposed, before the wave starts. This changes the spec-check prompt and its tests only.
findings_note: Owner 2026-11-03: slicer and ork should both encourage well defined acceptance criteria for every slice. Fact: ork prompts/spec-check.md asks only that a slice "names its checks" (line 40), so a vague Check passes. Needed: the spec check flags a slice whose Check or Failing tests do not say how to tell it is done (no command to run, no expected output or observable result, or a check the sandbox cannot run) and asks the owner to tighten it before the wave starts. Related: S277 (role briefs), slicer S102 (empty Check blocks next).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Owner 2026-11-03: slicer and ork should both encourage well defined acceptance criteria for every slice. Fact at HEAD of main (read 2026-11-05): `internal/roles/prompts/spec-check.md:38-41` makes a slice ready when it "names its files, its failing tests, its implementation steps and its checks". A Check that says only "tests pass" or "works as described" names a check and passes. The implementer then guesses what done means, and the reviewer and gate judge a bar nobody wrote down (wave 7, S277's Why). The slicer side is slicer's own (slicer S102, empty Check blocks the next step); this slice is the ork side and does not touch slicer.

Proposed design (the owner asked for "flag it and ask the owner to tighten it"; the option set below is proposed until the owner says otherwise):

- A check is verifiable when it is a command with an expected result (counts, exit status, output text or a file or state that can be observed), or a `[HUMAN CHECK]` item that says what the owner looks at and what they should see.
- A check is not verifiable when it has no command and no observable result ("works", "is clean", "tests pass" with no command), or its command cannot run in the implementer's sandbox (it needs a path or tool outside the allowlist; `DefaultImplementerAllowlist`, `internal/engine/perm.go:23-35`).
- Failing tests are verifiable when each is named and says what it asserts.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
In `internal/roles/roles_test.go:609-659`, beside `TestSpecCheckPrompt`:

- `TestSpecCheckPromptRequiresVerifiableCriteria`: readiness requires verifiable Failing tests and Check sections; reject no command and no observable result, commands the sandbox cannot run, and unnamed assertions. A `[HUMAN CHECK]` states what the owner looks at and should see. Fails first because step 2 only names checks.
- `TestSpecCheckPromptProposesTheWording`: one question per slice offers exactly tighten, human check and as written; tighten proposes a command and expected result and is recommended; omit Decision key. Fails first because this rule is absent.
- `TestSpecCheckPromptDoesNotAskWhatTheCodeSettles`: read the slice, Files and AGENTS.md, use an obvious project test command and result to call it ready, and ask only when these cannot settle the gap. Fails first because this guard is absent.
- Existing `TestSpecCheckPrompt` stays green (no VERDICT, [owner] or [fix], ASCII only).

In `internal/engine/speccheck_test.go:290-331`, beside `TestParseOwnerQuestionsReadsEveryBlock`:

- `TestSpecCheckCriteriaExampleBlockParses`: extract the worked vague-Check block from the actual prompt; ParseOwnerQuestions returns one question, exactly three options, recommendation and empty decision key. Fails first because the worked block is absent.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Tests first from the failing list; confirm each fails for the reason given.
2. In `spec-check.md` step 2, add a bullet: its `Failing tests` and `Check` each say how to tell it is done, as defined above. Add the three not-verifiable cases as a short list. Keep the existing bullets.
3. Add a short rule: when a slice fails this bullet and the command or result cannot be read from the slice, its Files or `AGENTS.md`, ask one question for that slice (not one for each vague line). Name the options `tighten`, `human check` and `as written`; put proposed command and expected result text in the `tighten` summary; recommend `tighten`. Omit the Decision key line: the answer belongs to this slice, not to a project-wide decision.
4. Add the worked question block to the report section, in the same strict shape as the existing example.
5. Do not change `CheckReport`, `ParseOwnerQuestions` or the engine's spec-check flow (`RecordSpecAnswers` already appends an answer to the slice's Implement section).
6. Keep the prompt ASCII and the placeholder list as they are (`TestPlaceholders`, `TestPromptsFirstLineNamesTheirContract` stay green).
7. Update `docs/design.md` in the same diff.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go -C WORKTREE test -count=1 ./internal/roles ./internal/engine -run 'SpecCheck|ParseOwnerQuestions|Placeholders|FirstLine'`: all pass.
- `go -C WORKTREE test -race -count=1 ./...`, `go -C WORKTREE vet ./...`, `gofmt -l WORKTREE` (empty), `slicer check`, `adj lint`.
- `rg -n 'HUMAN CHECK' internal/roles/prompts/spec-check.md` lists the new bullet and the option text.
- Mutation: remove the new bullet from `spec-check.md`; `TestSpecCheckPromptRequiresVerifiableCriteria` goes red. Remove the worked block; `TestSpecCheckCriteriaExampleBlockParses` goes red.
- [HUMAN CHECK] [AFTER LAND] Start a wave on a slice whose Check says only "works" (a throwaway filing): the spec check asks one question with the three options and a proposed command, and a well-specified slice still shows `Ready`.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch: "Spec check asks for verifiable acceptance criteria".
